newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty unchanged vs basket, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty unchanged vs basket, depos flat.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed a thin trading session unchanged against the currency basket as banks closed positions after this morning's light currency-buying on the back of small client orders and speculation, dealers said.

They said foreign investors purchased an estimated $40 million of Polish two- and five-year fixed bonds on Wednesday, which was likely to create some pro-zloty sentiment before the tender's settlement on March 12.
"We may see a growing supply of currencies (on the forex market) before the settlement date," said Katarzyna Tlenny, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 3.07/3.02 percent from the trading band centre, flat from Tuesday.
It was at 3.0780/95 to the dollar, down from 3.0730/45 on Tuesday and at 1.7965/75 to the mark, up from 1.7987/97.
Poland sold 226 million zlotys of 15-percent two-year bonds and only 40 million of 12-percent five year bonds after most bids for the longer paper were cut by the finance ministry.
Foreigners bought mostly two-year paper today, after purchasing five-year bonds at the last auction on February 5.
The minimum price of the two-year paper was cut to 90.21 from 90.60 but rose to 79.41 from 79.30 for the five-year bond.
One-day deposit rates were stable after the central bank drained excces money from the system by selling 401 million zlotys worth of NBP-bills and staging a 116 million zloty 14-day reverse repo.
Overnight deposit rates closed at 21.55/21.75 percent flat from opening's 21.50/21.90 percent. Tomorrow/next rates were at 21.65/21.85 percent versus 21.60/21.85 percent at 0915 GMT.
